newsitem.title: UK: P&O half-year results beat forecasts.
newsitem.headline: P&O half-year results beat forecasts.

text.p: Shipping and construction group Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co announced better than expected half-year results on Tuesday but warned of a difficult second half as the company gets to grips with its troubled container shipping and ferry businesses.

P&O said it made an underlying pre-tax profit of 130.2 million pounds ($202 million) on sales of 3.4 billion pounds for the six months to end-June, before adding a net gain of 4.5 million pounds on the sale of fixed assets.
Analysts forecasts had predicted pretax profits would drop back to 115-118 million pounds from last year's 131.9 million.
The company also revealed that it is to buy Nedlloyd NV's North Sea Ferries for 25.25 million pounds, the second deal between P&O and the Dutch group this month.
Nedlloyd and P&O announced last week they intend to merge their container shipping businesses into a $1.5 billion giant because of increasing global competition.
"Having announced an important step forward for containers we are now focusing on rationalising the ferry business," P&0 chairman Lord Sterling said on Tuesday. ($1=.6444 Pound)
